clue.text: Rather smart hedging tool

definitions.meaning: rather smart means neater or tidier, the comparative of an adjective for well turned out
a gardening device for cutting back hedges and edges

explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of trim (neat) and the name of a clipping machine for hedges are spelt the same.

clue.text: Give up and add the drier for nothing

definitions.meaning: to concede defeat, as a boxer's corner does
throw in means include free of charge, and a towel is a drier

explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's corner admits defeat by tossing a towel into the ring; read literally, the phrase means including a bathroom cloth free.

clue.text: I clear Irish leader with hesitation — it's elemental

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase meaning it is a chemical element, standing for the noun

parts.note: to rid is to clear, as in rid the house of mice

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Irish

parts.note: UM is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: A speaker hesitates while dismissing an Irish politician, declaring it basic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish leader' looks like a head of state; it is just the first letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard silvery metal, number 77 on the periodic table, is a chemical element.

clue.text: Little devil wants fruitcake with savoury nibble

parts.note: a monkey is a mischievous child, a little devil
a fruitcake is slang for a crazy person, as is nut

explanation.surface: A naughty child wants a slice of fruitcake alongside a salty snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruitcake' is slang for a crazy person, so NUT, not a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut in its shell is a savoury snack also sold under this name.

clue.text: Free to take tenants again

definitions.meaning: to let out a property on a fresh rental agreement

explanation.definitionFit: To let go is to set free, and a landlord who lets property afresh on a new rental contract does the same word hyphenated.

clue.text: Bother about little brother? How absurd!

indicators.note: about tells us the word for bother wraps around the word for a sibling

parts.note: to bother someone is to rile or annoy them
SIB is a short form of sibling, a brother or sister

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the silliness of being troubled by a small brother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little brother' is not a younger boy but a shortened word for a sibling; 'about' wraps the word for bother around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laughable or ridiculous is absurd.

clue.text: Just a lad given reparation

parts.note: just means fair or right
Ed is a boy's name, so a lad

explanation.surface: A fair-minded boy receives compensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'merely', but means fair: RIGHT. ED is any lad's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong that has been corrected or made good has been put right with compensation.

clue.text: Spots attracting tourists, say

indicators.note: say means the word for tourist attractions is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: places attracting tourists are the sights of a town

explanation.surface: Places that draw visitors, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it is the sound signal: the tourist sights, spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots are places or locations, and a location is also a site.

clue.text: They should ensure a roaring fire

definitions.text: They should ensure a roaring fire

parts.words: They should ensure a roaring fire
parts.note: a device that pumps air into a hearth keeps it blazing, and the same word also means roars loudly

explanation.surface: Something that keeps a hearth blazing nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roaring' hints at the second sense: the word also means loud roars.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-pumped device blows air into a fire to make it burn hotter.

clue.text: Figure it's always a threat to marriage

parts.note: something that is always there is eternal
a triangle is a geometric figure

explanation.surface: A geometric shape is said to be forever dangerous to wedded couples.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in reverse order: the figure comes first, but in the answer it follows the word for always.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair involving three people, two of them married, endangers a marriage.

clue.text: Hold sway in Niger, maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of Niger could be put in another possible order

explanation.surface: A ruler holds power in the African country of Niger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals that the five letters of NIGER can be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule as a monarch is to hold sway over a realm.

clue.text: Frivolous sportsman from Cambridge

parts.note: frivolous gives a word for not serious, and a Cambridge University sportsman is awarded his colours in that pale shade

explanation.surface: A not-so-serious athlete who studies at Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge at sport; Cambridge's colour is a pale shade, Oxford's dark, and the first word also means flippant or not serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge University sportsmen are called by the pale colour of their university, and the first word also means frivolous.

clue.text: Perfect fly fisherman may catch it

definitions.text: Perfect fly fisherman may catch it

parts.words: Perfect fly fisherman may catch it
parts.note: perfect suggests pure or spotless in colour and fly suggests a lure, together a small fish that a fisherman nets

explanation.surface: An expert angler who uses flies might hook a particular catch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'fly fisherman' together; split it so 'Perfect fly' is a spotless lure, while the tiny fish themselves are what a fisherman catches.
explanation.definitionFit: These tiny young fish, such as sprats and herrings, are netted by fishermen and eaten fried whole.

clue.text: Show contempt for small county

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
CORN is an abbreviation of Cornwall, a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a minor English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at the south-western tip of England, abbreviated CORN.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn someone is to treat them with disdain, a verb meaning to despise.

clue.text: No store confronts key agent

parts.note: a mine is a store or rich supply, as in a mine of information
E is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: An agent stands before a locked door with no shop behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is a musical key, not a door key; 'confronts' simply puts the first two pieces in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person put forward to act or stand for others is their representative, much like an agent.

clue.text: RAF officers engaged in trade merit dismissal

indicators.note: engaged in means the officers are occupied within the word for trade

parts.note: to trade is to deal, as in dealing goods
PO stands for Pilot Officer, an RAF rank, and POS is the plural

explanation.surface: Air force officers dabbling in commerce deserve to be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merit' is a link: the wordplay earns the definition. Pilot Officers are an RAF rank, and 'engaged in' puts them inside the word for trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Removal from office, especially of a ruler, is a dismissal from power.

clue.text: Made dean and prior decide in advance

indicators.note: made means created or formed, so the letters are fashioned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dean and a prior together settled matters beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made' looks like a past tense of the story, but it signals that DEAN and PRIOR are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain beforehand is to determine fate in advance, like predestine.

clue.text: Where Wolsey held court

parts.note: Cardinal Wolsey built a famous palace by the Thames, and court is both his royal gathering and the second word of the palace's name

explanation.surface: A historical question about where Cardinal Wolsey presided.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal Wolsey, Henry VIII's chief minister, built the palace on the Thames west of London known as ___ Court; 'held court' supplies the missing second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolsey's palace on the Thames, later taken by Henry VIII, takes this place name before the word Court.

clue.text: Screen a pupil in charge

definitions.meaning: a display screen, or as a verb to check or watch
a schoolchild given duties over others, such as a class prefect

explanation.definitionFit: A computer display screen and a school prefect-like pupil given duties share this name.

clue.text: Yank takes liquor back, the skinflint

definitions.note: the definition carries an article, but still means a miser

indicators.note: back means the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: to yank is to drag or pull hard
gin is an alcoholic liquor

explanation.surface: An American grabs a drink and refuses to share, the stingy so-and-so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' is not an American but the verb to pull, DRAG. 'back' turns DRAG + GIN into GARD + NIG, read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A miserly, mean person who hates spending is a skinflint.

clue.text: Railway supporter, but no activist

definitions.meaning: a wooden or concrete beam that holds up railway lines
someone inactive or dormant, like a spy waiting to be woken

explanation.definitionFit: Railway track rests on beams of this name, and a dormant agent or inactive person is also one.

clue.text: Dropped bombs without casing

definitions.meaning: with the hard outer covering removed, as with peas or nuts

explanation.definitionFit: Bombarding with explosives and removing peas from their pods share this word.

clue.text: Your hand may be her lifeline

definitions.text: Your hand may be her lifeline

parts.words: Your hand may be her lifeline
parts.note: a fortune-teller reads the lines of the hand, including the life line, so customers' hands are her living

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble may cling to a helping hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A lifeline is a rescue rope, but in hand-reading the life line is a crease on the palm; a reader of palms earns her living from your hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune-teller who reads the lines of the hand practises this trade.

clue.text: Present perhaps, but showing signs of stress

definitions.meaning: the present is an example of a grammatical time form for verbs, alongside past and future

explanation.definitionFit: Grammar's present is one verb form of time, and a strained, anxious person is also described by the same word.

clue.text: Some fear they've gone to ground

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people are afraid that the fugitives have gone into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone to ground' is a hunting term for a fox hiding in its den; the answer is the fox's hole, and as a verb means to drive into one.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox that goes to ground hides in its burrow, which is called by the same word.

clue.text: Freedom fighter is an utter brute

indicators.note: utter means say out loud, so the word for a brute is heard rather than written

parts.note: a gorilla is a large brutish ape

explanation.surface: A rebel is described as a complete savage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like an adjective meaning complete, but it is the verb: speak the word for the brute.
explanation.definitionFit: An irregular fighter in a resistance movement may call himself a freedom fighter.

clue.text: A raft well adapted for hazard on the river

indicators.note: adapted means changed or altered, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A raft that has been modified for dangers met on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' is not an adverb here but part of the fodder: A RAFT WELL rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade where a river drops steeply is a danger to boats.

clue.text: No good following a team that needs sacking

indicators.note: following places the abbreviation for no good after the team

parts.note: XI is the Roman numeral eleven, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A struggling football team deserves to have its players dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: A team of eleven players is written in Roman numerals in crosswords; 'following' puts the abbreviation for no good after A and the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting rid of staff, a dismissal, is a sacking.

clue.text: Tempted to go round church that's listed

indicators.note: go round means the word for tempted encircles the abbreviation for church

parts.note: to lure is to tempt, so tempted gives lured

explanation.surface: Someone is enticed to walk around a protected historic church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listed' suggests a protected building in Britain, but it means leaned to one side, like a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that lists leans over, so to have staggered or tilted suddenly is to have listed.

clue.text: Where English abstainer goes in to eat

indicators.note: goes in means the English abstainer is placed inside the verb for eating

parts.note: to dine is to eat a meal
TT means teetotal, so someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: Asking where a teetotal Englishman goes to have a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Teetotal is the crossword abstainer; 'goes in' sets English and the abstainer inside the verb, between its N and final E. 'Where' defines, with the rest of the clue painting a place to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dining area is a place where meals are taken.
